_doc: Haggling face to face at a market stall on the street map (player/haggling.js, ui/actionMenu/haggle.js). The keeper names a price from the market's own (Trading.buyCost / the sale Trading.sellGoods would make), moved by their mood and what they think of you (NpcDisposition.getPriceModifiers: disposition, traits, your name, your brand), their margin, how much they have, the hour (the last hours of the market sell cheaper, perishables most) and the tongue. You counter; each round costs their patience; push past it and they will not deal with you again that day (kept on the townsperson). The final price is that one transaction's: the goods and coin move exactly as the stall's trade does (the town's stock and purse). `bound` keeps any haggled price inside the buy-and-sell-back gap: a haggled buy never under what selling the lot straight back would fetch plus `buyGapShare` of the gap, a haggled sale never over the sale price plus `sellGapShare` of the gap to the buy-back cap (sellGapShare < buyGapShare: no loop). Fractions are of the list price.

openBuy: {price} for the {lot}. A fair price, and you know it.
For you? {price}. And I'm robbing myself.
openSell: {good}, is it? I'd give you {price} for the {lot}.
Let's see... {price}. That's as fair as I can do.
{price} for the {lot}, and I'm doing you a kindness.
openLate: Market's nearly done. {price} for the {lot}, and save me the carrying home.
Late in the day... call it {price}.
counterBuy: {offer}? Ha! {price}, and that's me being soft.
counterSell: {price}, and you're lucky to get it.
lowball: {offer}?! Are you mad, or just cheap?
That's daylight robbery! {price}, if you're serious.
accept: Done, and may you choke on the bargain!
grudging: {price}... you drive a hard bargain. Take it before I change my mind.
Done, curse you. Don't tell the others what you paid.
warm: A pleasure doing business. Come back soon!
Done! You've a good eye. Come again.
Done, and a fine day to you.
callback: Come back! {price}, and that's the last of it.
walked: Go on then. You'll not find better.
refuse: That's enough! Get away from my stall.
I'll not deal with you. Not today. Off with you!
Out! Go and haggle with the pigs.
spurned: We're done for the day, you and I.
flatterOk: You've a silver tongue. For you, {price}.
flatterFail: Sweet words don't feed my children.
Save your honey for the bees.
flawFail: There's nothing wrong with it! Look again.
Best in the square, and you know it.
praiseOk: Hm... it is good work. {price}, then.
praiseFail: Everyone says theirs is the best.
scoffFail: Go on then, try elsewhere. See if I care.
Threaten me at my own stall? The nerve.
crowd: They'll be at it all day.

you.flatter: Finest stall in the square, and the finest keeper.
you.praise: Look at the quality of these. You'll not see better this year.
you.scoff: You call that a price? I could do better at any stall in {town}.

flaws._doc: What you can find fault with at each trade's stall: [your line, ...].
greengrocer: Half of these are going soft.
There's mud and worse on these.
butcher: This is more gristle than meat.
Smells a day past its best.
fishmonger: The eyes are cloudy. Caught last week, was it?
baker: This loaf's a day old if it's an hour.
cheesemonger: There's mould on this, and not the good kind.
Sweating in the sun all day.
draper: This dye will run in the first rain.
potter: There's a crack in this glaze.
chandler: These candles are half tallow and smoke.
spicer: Gone stale. No smell to it.
vintner: This has turned. Vinegar by Sunday.
woodmonger: This is damp. It'll smoke, not burn.
any: I've seen better down the road.
